title: Connecting Cities With Minimum Cost
summary: Given n cities labeled from 1 to n and an array of connections where each connection is represented by [xi, yi, costi], determine the minimum total cost to connect all cities such that there is a path between every pair of cities.
statement: Given n cities labeled from 1 to n and an array of connections where each connection is represented by [xi, yi, costi], determine the minimum total cost to connect all cities such that there is a path between every pair of cities. If it is impossible to connect all cities, return -1. The cost is calculated as the sum of the costs of the selected connections.
constraints: Cities are labeled 1..n and connections are undirected weighted edges.
Return MST cost or -1 if not all cities connect.
hints: Kruskal chooses the cheapest edge that joins two current components.
Sort connections by cost and use union-find.
Accumulate successful unions; require exactly n-1.
The cut property proves every selected cheapest cross-component edge is safe for an MST.
editorial: The cut property proves every selected cheapest cross-component edge is safe for an MST.
